active_paradigms.idea: Exploit the exact threshold-to-bin-packing reduction with memoized branch-and-bound
active_paradigms.description: The current program is a greedy minimax constructor followed by only single moves and pairwise swaps, plus DIRECT over a discontinuous ordering/label decoder. Its key weakness is that DIRECT sees large flat regions and local improvement cannot perform coordinated multi-item ejection chains. For a candidate pressure threshold T, feasibility is exactly a bin-packing decision problem: a model i has transformed size a_i=w_i+T*s_i and every GPU has capacity 80*T, because load_g/(80-used_g)<=T iff sum_i assigned to g (w_i+T*s_i)<=80*T. Thus memory feasibility is automatically strict when weights are positive, but preserve an explicit original-size check for numerical safety. Binary-search T between a rigorous lower bound max(sum(w)/(gpu_num*80-sum(s)), max(w_i/(80-s_i))) and the incumbent pressure, and solve each decision problem by descending transformed-size placement with symmetry breaking. Memoize states consisting of the sorted remaining capacities and the next item index; try only distinct capacity values, largest fitting bins first, and stop at the first feasible packing. This is fundamentally global rather than a local-search neighborhood and directly optimizes the evaluator’s maximum KVPR, which is the quantity whose per-case values are averaged before reciprocal scoring. Return the best feasible threshold assignment, optionally retaining the incumbent as the initial upper bound only rather than running a second optimizer.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly reduce maximum KVPR on each evaluator case; especially improve dense cases where no beneficial one-model move or pair swap exists but a coordinated reassignment is feasible.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use a small positive memory margin because evaluator validity requires remaining memory, not merely nonnegative memory. Floating transformed capacities need rounded memoization keys or tolerance-aware canonicalization; do not merge genuinely different capacities too aggressively. Bound recursion/node count and fall back to the current feasible placement if a difficult instance exceeds the budget. The successful MILP/configuration principle was global threshold feasibility, but this avoids the previously retried scipy.optimize.milp formulation entirely.

active_paradigms.idea: Use maximum-weight matching to apply a whole compatible batch of exchanges rather than one greedy swap
active_paradigms.description: The existing improve routine evaluates every pair swap but commits only the single best swap, then repeats at most min(5,n) times. This can miss disjoint exchanges that must be made together: a swap may not lower the current maximum by itself, yet several swaps can lower all currently critical GPUs simultaneously. Build a graph whose vertices are candidate model positions on GPUs and whose edges represent feasible cross-GPU swaps. Give an edge a gain computed from the exact before/after pressures of its two affected GPUs, with substantially higher weight when it reduces a GPU tied for the current maximum. Call maximum_weight_matching with maxcardinality=False to select a vertex-disjoint set of exchanges in one global operation. Apply the proposed matching simultaneously, recompute the exact maximum KVPR, and accept it only if it improves the actual objective; otherwise discard it. Rebuild the graph after every accepted batch, including edges involving models on near-critical GPUs even when their isolated gain is zero. This preserves the current algorithm’s valid greedy initialization but replaces its myopic pair-swap commitment with a polynomial-size coordinated neighborhood.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape local minima caused by the current five-step, one-swap-at-a-time improvement loop and reduce the maximum, rather than merely average, per-GPU pressure.
active_paradigms.cautions: Edge gains are not truly additive because the objective is a maximum, so the matching is only a proposal and must always be checked against the exact full placement after simultaneous application. Only include swaps satisfying strict free-memory conditions in both directions. Avoid graph edges between models already on the same GPU, and use stable model indices because model objects may not be hashable. This is distinct from the prior combinations-based ejection-chain enumeration: it uses a single graph matching call to choose many disjoint exchanges globally.

active_paradigms.idea: Use linear assignment for cyclic one-model migrations across GPUs
active_paradigms.description: A useful neighborhood missing from the current code is a cycle such as A→B, B→C, C→A. No individual move may fit, and no pairwise swap need help, but the complete cycle can improve pressure and preserve memory. Select one migration candidate from each GPU, emphasizing models on GPUs at or near the maximum KVPR, and form a GPU-by-GPU cost matrix where assigning source GPU a’s selected model to destination b is forbidden unless b has enough residual memory after accounting for simultaneous departures. The cost for an allowed assignment should be a pressure-aware surrogate based on the destination’s post-arrival load/free ratio and a large penalty for retaining load on a critical source; diagonal entries represent no move. Solve this permutation in one call to linear_sum_assignment, which naturally permits cycles of any length rather than only swaps. Apply all non-diagonal assignments simultaneously, calculate the exact global maximum KVPR, and retain the result only when it is valid and strictly better. Repeat over a small deterministic set of candidate selections, such as largest-size, largest-weight, and highest individual w/(80-s) model from each critical GPU, rather than using a continuous optimizer. This directly addresses the discontinuous label search weakness of DIRECT while staying in a tractable assignment neighborhood.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Find feasible multi-GPU cyclic migrations that lower the bottleneck GPU KVPR when moves and pair swaps cannot cross intermediate memory barriers.
active_paradigms.cautions: The assignment surrogate is not the real minimax objective, so exact simultaneous memory and pressure validation is mandatory before accepting any result. Destination feasibility must use the final net size change, not the temporary state before its own selected model departs. Keep candidate selections few to maintain runtime, and preserve the best incumbent if all assignment proposals fail. This is not the failed differential-evolution/brute direct-label search: it is a deterministic polynomial cyclic-exchange subproblem with explicit final-state validation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve an exact set-partitioning formulation with scipy.optimize.milp over feasible GPU configurations
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses pressure-aware list scheduling: models are ordered by standalone pressure, each is placed on the GPU giving the lexicographically smallest sorted KVPR vector, and then at most five best-improving one-model moves or pairwise swaps are applied. Its strength is that it evaluates the true ratio objective for every tested greedy choice and preserves memory feasibility, but it can become trapped because the initial irreversible ordering and shallow neighborhood cannot perform coordinated rearrangements. For small or moderate model counts, enumerate every subset of models whose total model_size is at most 80 GB; each subset is a feasible configuration for one GPU, with a precomputed configuration KVPR equal to sum(req_rate/slo)/(80-sum(model_size)). Create one binary variable per configuration and use scipy.optimize.milp to select exactly gpu_num configurations while requiring every model to occur in exactly one selected configuration; include the empty configuration so unused GPUs are represented. Introduce a scalar z and impose z >= configuration_kvpr * selected_configuration for every configuration, then minimize z, which directly minimizes the testcase maximum KVPR rather than a proxy. This is globally optimal over the enumerated configuration set and attacks precisely the multi-model coordination missing from moves and swaps. The supplied wrapper only shows that evaluation delegates to evaluator.py, while the stated objective indicates each testcase placement should independently minimize its own maximum KVPR; no cross-test state should be retained.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimize each testcase's maximum GPU KVPR, which lowers the mean max-KVPR before the evaluator takes its reciprocal score transformation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Subset enumeration is exponential, so use this only when len(models) is sufficiently small or when model sizes permit aggressive pruning of infeasible subsets. Do not use rounded model sizes when checking the real 80 GB limit; the returned selected subsets must preserve exact model objects. Configurations with zero remaining memory have infinite pressure when they have positive load and should be excluded or assigned a prohibitively large coefficient. Ensure the MILP result is checked for success and retain a feasible greedy fallback if enumeration would be too large.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution with integer GPU-label variables and exact nonlinear memory constraints
tried_paradigms.description: Represent a placement by one integer variable per model, whose value is its GPU index, and evaluate it by recomputing every GPU's used memory, request load, and exact maximum KVPR. Unlike the current deterministic greedy construction, scipy.optimize.differential_evolution can change many assignments at once and therefore cross the local barriers that require several temporarily non-improving moves. Use its integrality argument so the search variables remain GPU labels, and impose one scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint per GPU requiring 80 minus that GPU's assigned total model_size to be nonnegative. The objective should be the maximum finite load/remaining-memory ratio, with a very large value for any infeasible or zero-denominator loaded GPU. Break GPU-label permutation symmetry by pinning a deterministic anchor model to GPU 0 or by canonicalizing labels inside objective evaluation; this avoids wasting most of the population on equivalent placements. Seed the initial population around the current pressure-aware greedy result plus diversified perturbations, so the existing strong heuristic remains useful while the global population search explores qualitatively different partitions. This is a direct discrete placement search, not tuning the parameters of another algorithm.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current five-iteration move/swap local optimum and optimize the actual maximum-ratio objective under exact memory constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This can be slower than the greedy method, especially with many models, so set a bounded population size and iteration budget consistent with evaluator time limits. Objective evaluation must tolerate empty GPUs, whose pressure is zero, and must never divide by a nonpositive residual capacity. Integer-label evolutionary search has substantial symmetry; failure to canonicalize or anchor labels can make it less reliable than the present heuristic. Return the best feasible decoded assignment only, not the floating optimizer vector.

tried_paradigms.idea: Expand local search to exact multi-model ejection chains enumerated with itertools.combinations
tried_paradigms.description: The present local search considers only a single relocation or a swap of one model on each side, accepts only strict immediate improvements, and repeats only min(5, number_of_models) times. Its greedy initialization is already effective because it compares the complete sorted KVPR profile, so a focused stronger neighborhood is likely simpler and safer than replacing all of it. Starting from that placement, enumerate small subsets of one to three models from the currently worst-pressure GPU using itertools.combinations, and test relocating that subset jointly to one or several destination GPUs whenever all destination memory constraints remain feasible. Also enumerate exchange chains such as worst GPU -> A, A -> B, B -> worst GPU, where each chain can exchange total size and total request weight in ways impossible for a pairwise swap. For every feasible candidate, recompute all changed GPUs' exact KVPRs and compare the full sorted pressure tuple, retaining the single lexicographically best strict improvement. Repeat until no improving chain exists rather than stopping after five rounds; accepting only strict tuple improvement guarantees termination and never degrades the primary maximum. This specifically repairs the current program's principal weakness: it cannot free enough memory on a desirable GPU to accept a high-load model unless every intermediate single move is beneficial and feasible.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the bottleneck GPU's KVPR through coordinated, memory-feasible reassignment while retaining the current algorithm's exact objective comparison and deterministic behavior.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Cap subset size at two or three and prioritize models from the worst one or two GPUs, otherwise combinatorial enumeration can exceed the evaluation budget. Apply and undo aggregate size/load deltas carefully; the current swap bookkeeping is delicate, and chain evaluation is safer if it uses copied aggregate arrays or a single centralized delta routine. Reject candidates with residual memory at or below zero when their resulting load is positive. Preserve model identity when updating placement lists, particularly if model objects have equal attributes.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the arbitrary subset cap with a stronger set-partitioning MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program enumerates every feasible GPU subset, then solves the correct minimax set-partitioning formulation with scipy.optimize.milp. Its principal weakness is the hard 12,000-configuration cutoff: once exceeded, it discards the exact formulation entirely and reverts to a one-pass greedy assignment, which is likely the main source of score loss. Retain the configuration formulation because it linearizes the otherwise bilinear KVPR objective exactly: every selected configuration has fixed pressure, and z only needs to dominate selected configuration pressures. Generate configurations by depth-first enumeration with models ordered by decreasing size, stop only on a wall-clock budget, and retain the best completed incumbent rather than immediately reverting to greedy when the configuration count grows. Remove duplicate configurations that have the same mask, and pass a valid greedy placement as an incumbent if the installed SciPy version supports it; otherwise use a moderate MILP time limit and accept any feasible solver result. Empty configurations must remain available because the evaluator may provide more GPUs than needed, but require exactly gpu_num selected configurations as in the current model. This directly attacks the evaluator's mean maximum-KVPR objective because it globally chooses co-located model groups rather than making irreversible per-model decisions.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Minimize the maximum configuration pressure exactly or near-exactly on cases where the current 12,000-subset threshold currently triggers greedy fallback; this is the primary quantity whose casewise mean is inverted by the evaluator.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not use a capacity condition that permits a positive-load group with zero remaining memory: require used memory to be strictly below 80 whenever its load is positive. A configuration is not safely removable merely because another configuration has lower pressure, since their model masks differ and exact cover constraints matter. Check result.success and that every model is covered exactly once before constructing output; otherwise return a validated heuristic placement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution with native integer assignment coordinates as a direct global minimax heuristic
tried_paradigms.description: Represent a placement by one integer coordinate per model, whose value is its GPU index, and evaluate it directly as the maximum KVPR after aggregating model sizes and request weights per GPU. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution with bounds [0, gpu_num-1] and its integrality argument so that candidates are true assignments rather than rounded continuous points. Return a very large finite penalty for any assignment that exceeds memory or leaves nonpositive residual memory for a GPU carrying positive request load; otherwise return the maximum KVPR. Initialize the population with several deterministic seeds implicitly encoded as an initial population only if the API permits it, especially the size-descending greedy placement and pressure-aware variants, then let this single global solver make coordinated reassignments. Unlike the current greedy fallback, mutation can move several models among GPUs together, escaping cases where a small model must be moved away before a large model can be placed beneficially. This is particularly useful when n is too large for subset enumeration but gpu_num is modest, where the search dimension is n rather than the exponential number of subsets. Validate the final assignment and use the best valid evaluated population member if the nominal returned point is penalized.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The direct maximum KVPR objective under memory feasibility on large instances where exact set partitioning cannot be constructed, improving the weak greedy branch rather than altering evaluator aggregation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a finite but decisively dominant infeasibility penalty, larger than any plausible valid KVPR, rather than infinity or NaN, because population optimizers can behave poorly with non-finite objectives. Set a strict time budget and deterministic seed for evaluator consistency. This is a heuristic, so retain a valid greedy placement as a safety fallback and compare objective values before accepting its output.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.brute for truly exact direct assignment search on small high-impact instances
tried_paradigms.description: For small instances, evaluate every GPU assignment directly with scipy.optimize.brute over n integer GPU-index ranges, using the real maximum-KVPR calculation as the objective. Invalid placements receive a large finite penalty, while valid placements receive max_g load_g divided by residual_memory_g. This solves the original assignment formulation without enumerating all feasible subsets or relying on a MILP numerical result, so it is an independent correctness backstop. It can be selected only when gpu_num ** n is safely below a fixed evaluation budget, for example a few hundred thousand to a few million objective evaluations depending on observed timing. On these small cases it guarantees the best attainable placement, including placements the current subset solver might miss if its configuration enumeration was cut off or its MILP terminates early. Because GPU labels are symmetric, fix the first model onto GPU 0 in the search parameterization when possible, reducing equivalent assignments by roughly gpu_num. Use this exact result only when it improves over the validated greedy or MILP candidate.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Obtain provably minimum maximum KVPR for small cases, preventing a few poorly placed small test instances from disproportionately worsening the mean KVPR and therefore the reciprocal evaluator score.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Never invoke exhaustive assignment search above a conservative cardinality threshold; its cost is exponential in model count. Ensure the objective treats unused GPUs as zero pressure and rejects any used GPU with residual memory at or below zero. GPU-label symmetry reduction must not remove valid solutions: fixing one arbitrary model to GPU 0 is safe because GPUs are identical.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.brute for exact symmetry-reduced GPU-label enumeration on small instances
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a configuration-set MILP: it enumerates every memory-feasible model subset, then selects exactly gpu_num subsets that partition models while minimizing the maximum precomputed subset pressure. Its principal weakness is that the 12,000-configuration cutoff switches abruptly to a one-pass greedy algorithm, so instances just beyond roughly 13 models may receive no global optimization at all. For small-to-moderate cases, call scipy.optimize.brute directly on integer GPU labels, with the first model fixed to GPU 0 and each later label restricted to at most one larger than the largest prior label; this removes GPU-permutation duplicates. The objective should decode labels, return infinity for any group with used memory greater than or equal to 80 GB, and otherwise return the exact maximum KVPR used by the evaluator. Because every canonical labeling is visited, this is an exact optimizer over placements rather than a relaxation or proxy. Use it only when the resulting canonical search space is below a conservative evaluation-time budget, and retain a deterministic constructive fallback for larger instances.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes each test case's exact maximum KVPR; since the printed score is the reciprocal of the mean of these per-case maxima, improving any case without harming others improves the primary scalar.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not optimize total pressure, variance, or a linearized denominator: the evaluator-facing quantity is the maximum of load/(80-used-memory). Empty GPUs are valid and have zero pressure. Keep the strict used-memory condition when the denominator would be zero or negative, and ensure all input models appear exactly once after decoding. scipy.optimize.brute is exponential, so its gating threshold must be based on gpu_num and model count, not merely model count.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing with a direct exact-placement objective and canonicalized labels
tried_paradigms.description: Treat a candidate vector as one GPU label per model and minimize the actual maximum KVPR after deterministic rounding and label canonicalization, using scipy.optimize.dual_annealing as the sole global search call. This differs from the current set-partitioning formulation because it searches assignments directly and never needs to materialize all feasible model subsets, avoiding the 12,000-subset cliff and the large sparse MILP construction. Assign a very large finite objective to memory-infeasible candidates, rather than allowing division by zero or NaN, and use the exact pressure formula for feasible assignments. Canonicalize labels by order of first occurrence before evaluation, so equivalent permutations of GPU IDs collapse to the same placement and the search has fewer redundant basins. Seed it deterministically for score stability and set the iteration budget from instance size. Decode the best returned vector directly into the required dictionary, including every GPU key even if it is empty.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact bottleneck KVPR for cases where exhaustive configuration enumeration is too large, particularly those currently sent to the simplistic size-first greedy fallback.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The decision space is discrete even though dual_annealing accepts real values; rounding must be deterministic and consistent between objective evaluation and final reconstruction. Penalties must dominate every feasible pressure but remain finite, since infinities can destabilize stochastic optimizers. This is a direct solver for placement, not a parameter tuner for a separate heuristic. Evaluate candidate feasibility after rounding, and never repair a candidate in a way that makes the evaluated objective differ from the returned placement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.direct on a feasibility-threshold formulation of KVPR minimization
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the key algebraic structure missing from the current greedy fallback: for a proposed maximum pressure T, every GPU must satisfy load/(80-used) <= T, equivalently load + T*used <= 80*T, while used remains below 80. Use scipy.optimize.direct to search a direct assignment encoding with an objective equal to the smallest violated threshold margin, or more simply the exact maximum KVPR with infeasible-memory penalties. DIRECT's deterministic partitioning is useful when reproducibility matters more than randomized exploration and it avoids both subset enumeration and a 30-second MILP solve. A strong encoding is a continuous priority value per model plus a GPU-choice coordinate, rounded deterministically to labels and canonicalized before scoring; model priorities can place larger models consistently before smaller ones during decoding if a feasibility-preserving decoder is part of that single objective evaluation. The final value must still be recomputed as the exact maximum pressure of the decoded placement, not the threshold surrogate. This targets the difficult mixed memory/load tradeoff: a large model reduces denominator sharply, whereas a high request-rate model raises numerator sharply, and neither is captured well by sorting solely by size and weight.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The bottleneck pressure and, specifically, placements where balancing raw request load is harmful because remaining memory denominators differ substantially among GPUs.
tried_paradigms.cautions: DIRECT is a black-box search over a discontinuous rounded assignment map, so bound dimensions tightly and use a finite call budget appropriate to evaluation time. The threshold inequality is valid only for positive remaining memory; configurations with exactly 80 GB used must be rejected, not treated as a finite-pressure placement. Do not report the surrogate margin as the objective or omit empty GPU entries. Ensure any priority-based decode is deterministic, so the scored candidate and final placement are identical.
